scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budget_for_an_.purpose: Opens one account's budget within a budget version to see its monthly amounts, notes and how it was built — for example the monthly phasing of 6620 Real Estate Taxes.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budget_for_an_.outcome: The accountant can explain exactly what was budgeted for an account when a variance question arrives.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budget_for_an_.rootCause: Variance explanations start with 'what did we budget and why'. Seeing the account's budget detail and notes in one place answers that without digging through budget-season spreadsheets.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_budget_for_an_.ifSkipped: Variance commentary is written without knowing the budget assumption, and explanations to the asset manager are guesses.
redFlags: Budget lines without notes explaining the assumption

scr_budgeting_adding_budget_details_for_.purpose: Adds budget amounts for an account that was left out of a budget version — typically an account created mid-year or one the property manager forgot to budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_details_for_.outcome: The account is budgeted so BVA reports compare its actuals to a real plan instead of zero.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_details_for_.rootCause: Accounts with actual activity but no budget produce 100% variances every month, which generate repeated questions from the asset manager and hide real performance issues.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_details_for_.ifSkipped: Unbudgeted accounts show recurring 100% variances that nobody can meaningfully explain.
redFlags: Budget added to the approved version without owner approval

scr_budgeting_editing_budget_details_for.purpose: Changes one account's budget amounts or phasing in a budget version — for example re-phasing the insurance budget to match a new policy renewal month.
scr_budgeting_editing_budget_details_for.outcome: The account's budget reflects the approved plan with correct monthly timing.
scr_budgeting_editing_budget_details_for.rootCause: Phasing errors (an annual premium budgeted in one month instead of monthly amortization) produce large, meaningless monthly variances even when the annual total is right.
scr_budgeting_editing_budget_details_for.ifSkipped: Monthly variance reports show large swings that net to zero over the year but consume review time every month.
gaap: ASC 340-10 — prepaid expense amortization (drives monthly phasing)
redFlags: Edits to an approved budget without a documented approval

scr_budgeting_budget_periods_list.purpose: Lists the periods (months) of a budget with their amounts for the selected account, used to review and edit phasing across the fiscal year.
scr_budgeting_budget_periods_list.outcome: Monthly phasing is visible and editable in one list.
scr_budgeting_budget_periods_list.rootCause: Budgets must match the property's seasonal pattern — higher utilities in summer, more turnover costs in peak leasing season — so monthly variances reflect real performance.
scr_budgeting_budget_periods_list.ifSkipped: Flat phasing makes every seasonal month look like a variance.
redFlags: Seasonal accounts budgeted evenly across months

scr_budgeting_budget_amount_details_page.purpose: The page for adding or editing an account's budget amounts by period, with any supporting information about how the amount was derived.
scr_budgeting_budget_amount_details_page.outcome: Budget amounts entered with their rationale attached.
scr_budgeting_budget_amount_details_page.rootCause: Recording the basis of each budget amount (per-unit rate, contract amount, escalator) at entry makes the budget defensible when the asset manager challenges it months later.
scr_budgeting_budget_amount_details_page.ifSkipped: Budget amounts exist without rationale and cannot be defended in variance discussions.
redFlags: Large budget amounts without supporting notes

scr_budgeting_adding_information_about_t.purpose: Adds descriptive information to an account's budget — assumptions, contract references, per-unit calculations — to accompany the numbers.
scr_budgeting_adding_information_about_t.outcome: Budget assumptions are documented where reviewers and variance writers will see them.
scr_budgeting_adding_information_about_t.rootCause: Assumptions documented in the system survive staff turnover; assumptions kept in a preparer's head or email do not.
scr_budgeting_adding_information_about_t.ifSkipped: When the preparer leaves, nobody knows why a line was budgeted as it was.
redFlags: Assumption notes missing on material lines

scr_budgeting_entering_budget_amounts_fo.purpose: Enters budget amounts for each reporting period of the fiscal year for an account, either individually or by spreading an annual amount.
scr_budgeting_entering_budget_amounts_fo.outcome: Complete monthly budget amounts for the account.
scr_budgeting_entering_budget_amounts_fo.rootCause: BVA reporting compares monthly actuals to monthly budgets; missing periods show as full variances and partial-year budgets understate the annual plan.
scr_budgeting_entering_budget_amounts_fo.ifSkipped: Some months have no budget and show full variances.
redFlags: Months with zero budget on recurring expense accounts

scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_budget_check_.purpose: Configures the approval workflow to check A/P invoices and purchase orders against the remaining budget for the GL line before approval.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_budget_check_.outcome: Approvers see, at the moment of approval, whether a transaction will push the line over budget.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_budget_check_.rootCause: Owners delegate spend within an approved budget. Catching over-budget spend at approval — rather than in next month's BVA — is the preventive control that keeps the management company within its authority.
scr_budgeting_setting_up_a_budget_check_.ifSkipped: Over-budget spend is discovered only after it is incurred and owners dispute reimbursing it.
redFlags: Budget check pointing at a draft budget rather than the approved one

scr_budgeting_setting_a_system_action_wh.purpose: Sets what the system does when a transaction exceeds its budget — warn the approver, require an additional approver, or prevent the transaction.
scr_budgeting_setting_a_system_action_wh.outcome: Over-budget spend is handled according to the owner's delegation of authority.
scr_budgeting_setting_a_system_action_wh.rootCause: Different owners set different tolerances: some want a hard stop on unbudgeted capex, others only a warning on small opex overruns. The system action encodes that policy.
scr_budgeting_setting_a_system_action_wh.ifSkipped: All overruns are treated the same, either blocking routine operations or letting material unbudgeted spend through.
redFlags: Warn-only settings on capital lines the owner requires hard stops for

scr_budgeting_bypassing_budget_checks.purpose: Allows specific transactions or accounts to bypass budget checks — for example non-controllable items like real estate taxes or emergency repairs where blocking payment would cause harm.
scr_budgeting_bypassing_budget_checks.outcome: Essential payments are not held up by budget controls designed for discretionary spend.
scr_budgeting_bypassing_budget_checks.rootCause: Some costs are not controllable (tax bills, utility bills) and delaying them causes penalties or service cut-offs. Bypass rules keep the control focused on discretionary spend — but bypasses must be limited and reviewed.
scr_budgeting_bypassing_budget_checks.ifSkipped: Either essential payments are blocked, or bypasses are granted too broadly and the budget control stops working.
redFlags: Bypass applied to discretionary accounts such as marketing

scr_budgeting_working_budgets_list.purpose: Lists working budgets in Forecasting & Planning — drafts, revisions and reforecasts by year and property — with their status and publish history.
scr_budgeting_working_budgets_list.outcome: A clear register of every budget version in progress and which have been published to the GL.
scr_budgeting_working_budgets_list.rootCause: Budget season produces many drafts per property. Without a register, teams edit the wrong draft or publish an unapproved version.
scr_budgeting_working_budgets_list.ifSkipped: Wrong drafts are edited or published, and BVA reports use an unapproved budget.
redFlags: Multiple working budgets for the same property and year marked active

scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget.purpose: Creates a working budget for one or more properties and a fiscal year, seeded from actuals, a prior budget or blank.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget.outcome: A draft budget ready for assumptions and review.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget.rootCause: Working budgets separate drafting from the approved GL budget, so property managers can iterate without affecting reporting.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Drafting happens in spreadsheets outside the system.
redFlags: Working budgets seeded from partial-year actuals

scr_budgeting_editing_a_working_budget.purpose: Edits a working budget's amounts and assumptions during review cycles with the regional and asset managers.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_working_budget.outcome: The draft reflects agreed changes from each review round.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_working_budget.rootCause: Budgets go through several review rounds; changes must be applied to the working budget so the final version is complete.
scr_budgeting_editing_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Agreed review changes are lost and the final budget differs from what was agreed.
redFlags: Edits after the budget was published

scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget.purpose: Views a working budget's header, properties and status, and opens its details, summary and publish history.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget.outcome: A quick check of a draft's state before editing or publishing.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget.rootCause: Before editing or publishing, the accountant must confirm it is the right draft for the right properties and year.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Edits or a publish are applied to the wrong draft, and the owner-approved numbers are overwritten.
redFlags: Drafts without clear version names

scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget_s.purpose: Shows the working budget summarized by account or account group with totals, used to review the budget at a glance.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget_s.outcome: A high-level view to check totals like revenue, controllable expenses and NOI before line review.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget_s.rootCause: Reviewers start with totals (is NOI growth reasonable?) before diving into lines; the summary provides that view.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budget_s.ifSkipped: Line-level reviews miss that the overall NOI is unrealistic.
redFlags: NOI growth inconsistent with market assumptions

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.purpose: Shows when a working budget was published to the GL budget, by whom and to which budget.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.outcome: An audit trail of what was published and when.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.rootCause: If BVA numbers change unexpectedly, the publish history shows whether the budget was republished and by whom.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.ifSkipped: Unexpected budget changes cannot be traced.
redFlags: Republishing after owner approval without re-approval

scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.purpose: Deletes or inactivates a working budget draft that has been abandoned or superseded — for example the property manager's first draft once the regional manager's revision is final.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.rootCause: Abandoned drafts left active look like real options; under deadline, someone edits or publishes the stale draft and the GL budget no longer matches what the owner approved.
scr_budgeting_deleting_or_inactivating_a.ifSkipped: Old drafts are edited or published in error.
redFlags: Deleting the draft that was published

scr_budgeting_working_budget_page.purpose: The working budget record page — header, properties, fiscal year, status and links to details, summary and history.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_page.outcome: Central record for one budget draft.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_page.rootCause: A single record page keeps a draft's identity, scope and status clear across review rounds.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_page.ifSkipped: Drafts lose track of their scope and status, and teams cannot tell which one is approved.
redFlags: Status not updated after approval

scr_budgeting_duplicating_a_working_budg.purpose: Copies a working budget to create a new draft — for example to prepare the regional manager's revision while keeping the property manager's original draft.
scr_budgeting_duplicating_a_working_budg.outcome: Each review round has its own version for comparison.
scr_budgeting_duplicating_a_working_budg.rootCause: Keeping each round's version allows changes to be shown to the asset manager and reversed if needed.
scr_budgeting_duplicating_a_working_budg.ifSkipped: Earlier versions are overwritten and changes cannot be explained.
redFlags: Duplicates without distinguishing names

scr_budgeting_advance_actuals_box.purpose: Dialog to advance year-to-date actuals into a working budget or forecast, replacing budget amounts for completed months with actual results.
scr_budgeting_advance_actuals_box.outcome: Reforecasts show actual results for completed months plus projections for the rest of the year.
scr_budgeting_advance_actuals_box.rootCause: A 6+6 or 9+3 reforecast is only credible if the completed months are actuals; advancing actuals does that automatically.
scr_budgeting_advance_actuals_box.ifSkipped: Reforecasts mix budget and actual months manually with errors.
redFlags: Actuals advanced before the month was closed

scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.purpose: Procedure to pull closed-month actuals into a reforecast working budget through a chosen month.
scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.rootCause: Investors and lenders get reforecasts that must reconcile to reported actuals; advancing from the GL ensures that.
scr_budgeting_advancing_year_to_date_act.ifSkipped: Reforecast actuals differ from reported financials.
redFlags: Advancing into unclosed periods

scr_budgeting_working_budget_summary_pag.purpose: The page summarizing a working budget by account with totals by period, where users filter, add accounts, adjust and publish.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_summary_pag.outcome: The main editing and review surface for a draft budget.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_summary_pag.rootCause: Budget review needs totals, line detail and adjustment tools together to iterate quickly during budget season.
scr_budgeting_working_budget_summary_pag.ifSkipped: Budget work moves to disconnected spreadsheets and the system version falls out of date.
redFlags: Publishing from the summary without final review

scr_budgeting_filtering_the_working_budg.purpose: Filters the working budget summary by property, account group, dimension or period to focus the review.
scr_budgeting_filtering_the_working_budg.outcome: Reviewers look at one slice (e.g., payroll for one property) at a time.
scr_budgeting_filtering_the_working_budg.rootCause: Reviewing hundreds of lines at once is ineffective; filtering by group keeps reviews focused and consistent across properties.
scr_budgeting_filtering_the_working_budg.ifSkipped: Reviews are unfocused and important lines are missed.
redFlags: Filters hiding lines at publish time

scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.purpose: Adds a GL account to a working budget that did not come through the seed — for example a new income account for EV charging.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.outcome: New revenue or cost lines are budgeted.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.rootCause: Seeds based on prior actuals omit accounts with no history; new activities must be added explicitly.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_account_to_a_wor.ifSkipped: New activities are unbudgeted and show as variances all year.
redFlags: Known new activities missing from the budget

scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budgets_.purpose: Views one account's details in a working budget — periods, amounts, calculation method and comments.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budgets_.outcome: Line-level understanding of how an account was budgeted.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budgets_.rootCause: Reviewers need to see the method (actuals × escalator, per-unit rate) to evaluate a line.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_working_budgets_.ifSkipped: Lines are approved without understanding the method.
redFlags: Lines with no stated method

scr_budgeting_editing_an_accounts_detail.purpose: Edits the monthly amounts, calculation method or comments for a single account inside a working budget — the normal way to apply a reviewer's line-level feedback.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_accounts_detail.outcome: Individual lines corrected per review feedback.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_accounts_detail.rootCause: Reviewers change specific lines; edits must be made in the working budget to flow to the published version.
scr_budgeting_editing_an_accounts_detail.ifSkipped: Feedback is not reflected in the published budget.
redFlags: Edits without comments explaining the change

scr_budgeting_importing_workflow.purpose: Describes the import workflow for working budgets: download the template, fill it in Excel, import, and review results.
scr_budgeting_importing_workflow.outcome: Large budgets loaded consistently from spreadsheets.
scr_budgeting_importing_workflow.rootCause: Many property managers build budgets in Excel; a defined import workflow brings them into the system without re-keying.
scr_budgeting_importing_workflow.ifSkipped: Budgets are re-keyed from Excel with errors, and the system budget never matches the owner file.
redFlags: Imports not reconciled to the source file totals

scr_budgeting_downloading_or_exporting_a.purpose: Downloads the import template (or exports the current budget in template format) for filling in budget data offline.
scr_budgeting_downloading_or_exporting_a.outcome: A correctly structured file for importing budget data.
scr_budgeting_downloading_or_exporting_a.rootCause: Imports fail or load wrongly when files do not match the expected layout; starting from the template avoids that.
scr_budgeting_downloading_or_exporting_a.ifSkipped: Imports fail or map data to wrong accounts.
redFlags: Custom files used instead of the template

scr_budgeting_importing_data_into_a_work.purpose: Imports budget amounts from a completed import template into a working budget, loading hundreds of account-by-month values for one or more properties in one step.
scr_budgeting_importing_data_into_a_work.outcome: Budget data from spreadsheets loaded accurately.
scr_budgeting_importing_data_into_a_work.rootCause: Property managers typically build their numbers in Excel. Importing brings them into the system exactly as prepared, whereas re-keying hundreds of lines per property during budget season guarantees transcription errors.
scr_budgeting_importing_data_into_a_work.ifSkipped: Budgets are keyed by hand with errors that later appear as unexplained variances.
redFlags: Rows rejected by the import not followed up

scr_budgeting_exporting_a_working_budget.purpose: Exports a working budget to Excel for offline review by the regional or asset manager, labeled with the draft name and export date so comments come back on the right version.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_working_budget.outcome: The draft shared in Excel with clear version identity.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_working_budget.rootCause: Owners review budgets in Excel; exports must be labeled with version and date to avoid comments on the wrong draft.
scr_budgeting_exporting_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Owners comment on the wrong draft and agreed changes are applied to a different version.
redFlags: Exports without version labels

scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.purpose: Publishes an approved working budget to a General Ledger budget so it becomes the budget used by BVA reports and budget checks.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.outcome: The owner-approved budget becomes the official budget in the GL.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.rootCause: Publishing is the control point between drafting and reporting; only the approved version should be published, and publishing twice can overwrite the official budget.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_working_budge.ifSkipped: BVA reports and budget checks run against no budget or a draft.
redFlags: Publishing before owner approval
Publishing to the wrong GL budget

scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_for_a_.purpose: Removes an account from a working budget — for example an account that should not be budgeted at this property.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_for_a_.outcome: Irrelevant accounts removed from the draft.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_for_a_.rootCause: Seeds sometimes include accounts not relevant to the property (e.g., commercial accounts at a pure multifamily site).
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_account_for_a_.ifSkipped: Irrelevant lines clutter the budget and reports.
redFlags: Removing accounts that receive actual activity

scr_budgeting_account_detail_page.purpose: The account detail page within a working budget for entering amounts by period, applying calculations and adding comments.
scr_budgeting_account_detail_page.outcome: Complete line-level budget information for one account.
scr_budgeting_account_detail_page.rootCause: Recording the calculation method and comments next to each account's monthly amounts makes every budget line explainable months later, when a variance question arrives and the original preparer may have moved on.
scr_budgeting_account_detail_page.ifSkipped: Lines lack method and rationale, so variance explanations become guesswork.
redFlags: Amounts without comments

scr_budgeting_adding_budget_amounts_for_.purpose: Enters monthly budget amounts by hand for one account in a working budget — used for known items like a signed landscaping contract or a planned exterior paint project.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_amounts_for_.outcome: The account's budget populated with correct phasing.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_amounts_for_.rootCause: Some accounts need hand-entered amounts (a known contract, a planned project) rather than calculated ones.
scr_budgeting_adding_budget_amounts_for_.ifSkipped: Known, contracted costs are left out of the budget and show as full variances when they are incurred.
redFlags: Amounts entered in the wrong months

scr_budgeting_importing_budget_data_for_.purpose: Imports budget data for one account from a file, used when a detailed schedule (e.g., a payroll or contract schedule) is prepared separately.
scr_budgeting_importing_budget_data_for_.outcome: Detailed schedules loaded accurately into one budget line.
scr_budgeting_importing_budget_data_for_.rootCause: Detailed schedules for specific lines are often built outside the system; importing preserves their accuracy.
scr_budgeting_importing_budget_data_for_.ifSkipped: Detailed schedules are re-keyed with errors.
redFlags: Imported totals different from the schedule

scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.purpose: Calculates an account's budget as a percentage or amount increase over a base (prior budget or actuals) — for example insurance at +15% over the current premium.
scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.rootCause: Many budget lines follow escalators set by the asset manager (payroll +4%, insurance +15%); calculating them in the system keeps them consistent and traceable.
scr_budgeting_calculating_the_budget_inc.ifSkipped: Escalators are applied inconsistently across properties.
redFlags: Escalators applied to the wrong base year

scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.purpose: Adjusts one account's working budget by an amount or percentage after review feedback — for example 'reduce marketing by 10%' from the asset manager.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.rootCause: Review feedback is often a specific adjustment ('cut marketing 10%'); applying it directly is faster and less error-prone than recalculating by hand.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.ifSkipped: Adjustments are recalculated by hand with errors.
redFlags: Adjustments without comments

scr_budgeting_adding_a_comment_to_an_acc.purpose: Adds a comment to an account's budget explaining its assumptions or a review change.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_comment_to_an_acc.outcome: Budget rationale travels with the numbers.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_comment_to_an_acc.rootCause: Comments are what allow variance writers months later to explain why a line was set as it was.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_comment_to_an_acc.ifSkipped: Rationale is lost and variance explanations are weak.
redFlags: Material lines without comments

scr_budgeting_filtering_by_dimension_or_.purpose: Filters a working budget by dimension or segment (e.g., department, building, cost center) to review or budget at that level.
scr_budgeting_filtering_by_dimension_or_.outcome: Budgets reviewed or built by department or building.
scr_budgeting_filtering_by_dimension_or_.rootCause: Large properties budget by department or building; filtering by dimension supports that level of planning.
scr_budgeting_filtering_by_dimension_or_.ifSkipped: Department-level budgets are not possible in the system.
redFlags: Dimensions left blank on budget lines

scr_budgeting_adjustment_box.purpose: Dialog for applying an adjustment to selected budget lines — a percentage or amount, to certain periods or all.
scr_budgeting_adjustment_box.outcome: Consistent adjustments across multiple lines at once.
scr_budgeting_adjustment_box.rootCause: Top-down changes from the asset manager ('reduce all controllable expenses 3%') need to be applied uniformly.
redFlags: Adjustments applied to non-controllable lines

scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.purpose: Applies one adjustment across many accounts or properties in a working budget at once — for example updating every property's insurance line for a new portfolio insurance program cost.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.outcome: Portfolio-wide changes applied in one step.
scr_budgeting_adjusting_a_working_budget.rootCause: Portfolio-level assumptions (e.g., updated insurance program cost) affect many properties; bulk adjustment keeps them consistent.
redFlags: Bulk adjustments applied twice

scr_budgeting_publish_working_budget_his.purpose: Dialog showing the publish history of a working budget — dates, users and target budgets.
scr_budgeting_publish_working_budget_his.outcome: Visibility of when and where a draft was published.
scr_budgeting_publish_working_budget_his.rootCause: When BVA figures change unexpectedly mid-year, the first question is whether someone republished the budget. The publish history answers who published, when, and to which GL budget.
scr_budgeting_publish_working_budget_his.ifSkipped: Budget changes in reports cannot be explained.
redFlags: Multiple publishes after approval

scr_budgeting_payroll.purpose: Section on payroll planning in Forecasting & Planning — budgeting site staff wages, overtime, payroll taxes, benefits and workers' compensation by position and employee.
scr_budgeting_payroll.outcome: A detailed, defensible payroll budget, typically the largest controllable expense at a property.
scr_budgeting_payroll.rootCause: Payroll is often 25-35% of multifamily operating expenses and is heavily scrutinized by owners. Budgeting it by position with burden rates is far more accurate than escalating last year's total.
scr_budgeting_payroll.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets miss burden changes (tax rate, benefits, workers' comp) and produce large variances.
redFlags: Payroll budgets without burden

scr_budgeting_payroll_planning_workflow.purpose: Describes the payroll planning workflow: set up workers' comp classes, job positions, employees, tax rates and benefits; calculate payroll; publish it to the working budget.
scr_budgeting_payroll_planning_workflow.outcome: Payroll budget built from its components in the right order.
scr_budgeting_payroll_planning_workflow.rootCause: Payroll depends on several tables; building in the wrong order (calculating before rates are set) gives wrong results.
scr_budgeting_payroll_planning_workflow.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets calculated on missing or old rates.
redFlags: Payroll calculated before tax rates updated for the new year

scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.purpose: Lists workers' compensation classes (e.g., clerical, maintenance, building operations) with rates used to budget workers' comp by position.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.outcome: Workers' comp budgeted by risk class rather than a flat percentage.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.rootCause: Maintenance staff carry much higher workers' comp rates than office staff; budgeting by class reflects the real cost.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.ifSkipped: Workers' comp is under-budgeted for maintenance-heavy properties.
redFlags: Maintenance positions assigned clerical class

scr_budgeting_adding_a_worker_compensati.purpose: Adds a workers' compensation class code with its premium rate (per $100 of payroll) so positions assigned to it are budgeted at the right workers' comp cost.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_worker_compensati.rootCause: Expanding into a new state or adding a new position type (e.g., a pool attendant) can require a class code with a different rate. Without it, those positions borrow an unrelated class and their burden is misstated.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_worker_compensati.ifSkipped: Positions use inappropriate classes and rates.
redFlags: Rates not updated for the new policy year

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_worker.purpose: Views or updates workers' comp class rates — typically at policy renewal each year.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_worker.outcome: Payroll budgets use current workers' comp rates.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_worker.rootCause: Workers' compensation rates reset at each policy renewal and can move significantly after claims. Budgets built on last year's rates misstate one of the largest payroll burden components.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_worker.ifSkipped: Payroll burden is misstated and payroll variances appear all year.
redFlags: Rates from prior policy year

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_worker_compensa.purpose: Deletes a workers' compensation class that no position uses any more, such as a class for a state the company no longer operates in.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_worker_compensa.outcome: Only relevant class codes remain available for assignment.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_worker_compensa.rootCause: Unused classes may be selected by mistake for new positions, applying wrong rates.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_worker_compensa.ifSkipped: Obsolete classes are selected for new positions and their outdated rates flow into the payroll budget.
redFlags: Deleting classes still assigned to positions

scr_budgeting_copying_records_from_a_pre.purpose: Copies payroll setup records (classes, positions, taxes, benefits) from the prior year into the new budget year.
scr_budgeting_copying_records_from_a_pre.outcome: Payroll setup carried forward, needing only rate updates.
scr_budgeting_copying_records_from_a_pre.rootCause: Most payroll setup is stable year to year; copying saves time, but rates must then be updated to avoid budgeting at last year's costs.
scr_budgeting_copying_records_from_a_pre.ifSkipped: Setup is rebuilt from scratch each year.
redFlags: Copied records not updated for new rates

scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.purpose: The page for entering or editing one workers' compensation class — class code, description and premium rate per $100 of payroll — used by every position assigned to it.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.outcome: Accurate class definitions for payroll budgeting.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.rootCause: The rate on this page multiplies across every position in the class, so a single entry error (for example 5.2 entered as 52) inflates workers' comp for every maintenance position in the portfolio.
scr_budgeting_worker_compensation_class_.ifSkipped: Rate errors spread across all positions in the class.
redFlags: Rates entered as whole numbers instead of per $100 of payroll
